  "purpose": "Define how Callisto finds the workspace root, decides which manifests are packages, gives each package an identity, applies per-package config, and treats npm platform packages.",
  "scope": "Workspace root detection, project discovery and membership, package identity and dependency edges, [[package]]/[[package-set]] resolution, and npm platform packages.",
  "non_goals": [

  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-01",
      "criterion": "Root detection walks up from the start directory, never past the Git toplevel, and picks the nearest directory with a workspace marker (Cargo.toml with [workspace], package.json with `workspaces`, pnpm-workspace.yaml, or a .moon directory); with no marker it picks the outermost directory with a package manifest (Cargo.toml with [package], package.json, or pyproject.toml)."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-02",
      "criterion": "Root detection fails with E030 naming the start directory and Git toplevel when no marker or package manifest exists up to the toplevel, and with E058 (help suggests `git init`) when the start directory is not inside a Git repository.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-03",
      "criterion": "Discovery treats every directory under the root whose Cargo.toml, package.json or pyproject.toml parses and declares a package name as a candidate, following symlinks up to 32 levels deep and skipping hidden and gitignored paths and directories named target, node_modules, .git, .moon and dist; a manifest without a name is not a package.     },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-04",
      "criterion": "A Cargo candidate is admitted when the root Cargo.toml [workspace] has no `members` key or its path matches `members`, and its path does not match `exclude`; Python candidates follow the same rules using pyproject.toml [tool.uv.workspace]."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-05",
      "criterion": "Membership globs match root-relative paths where `*` matches one path segment, `**` matches any depth, and an entry starting with `!` removes matching paths from the list's other entries."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-06",
      "criterion": "With no root manifest or no workspace table for an ecosystem, every candidate of that ecosystem is admitted; an empty `members`, `workspaces` or `packages` list admits none except a hybrid root."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-07",
      "criterion": "An npm candidate is admitted when its path matches the `packages` list of the root pnpm-workspace.yaml, or, when that file is absent or unusable, the root package.json `workspaces` array; with neither, all npm candidates are admitted."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-08",
      "criterion": "A hybrid root (root Cargo.toml with both [package] and [workspace], root pyproject.toml with both [project] and [tool.uv.workspace], or a root package.json with a `name`) is always admitted, even when `exclude` matches `.` or the member globs do not.     },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-09",
      "criterion": "Malformed membership input never fails discovery: an unparseable root manifest or a `members`, `workspaces` or `packages` value that is not an array of strings is treated as absent, an unparseable, empty or `packages`-less pnpm-workspace.yaml falls back to package.json `workspaces`, and a malformed `exclude` excludes nothing.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-DISC-10",
      "criterion": "An invalid glob in `members`, `exclude`, `workspaces` or `packages` is ignored while the list's valid entries still apply.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-01",
      "criterion": "A package whose name is claimed by no other directory gets a bare id equal to its manifest name (for example `foo` or `@scope/foo`)."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-02",
      "criterion": "A dual-manifest package (one directory with several admitted manifests) is one package whose id comes from Cargo.toml, else package.json, else pyproject.toml, and each manifest's own name still resolves to that package within its ecosystem -- including through `--package`, `add` and a changeset entry naming the package by a non-primary manifest's own name, not only its primary name."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-03",
      "criterion": "When two or more directories declare the same name and no ecosystem declares it in more than one of them, each package is promoted to an ecosystem-qualified id, displayed as `cargo/foo`. Newly created default tags use `{display id}@{version}`, so promotion changes their namespace. A promoted package's last tag is also found among `foo@*` tags whose commit contains its manifest and no other same-named package's. A bare `pre.json` `initialVersions` key moves to the one same-named package that existed when `pre.json` was added, else `version` fails with E245."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-04",
      "criterion": "When two directories declare the same name in the same ecosystem (including a dual-manifest Cargo+npm `foo` and an npm-only `foo`), loading fails with E100 naming both paths.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-05",
      "criterion": "A `[[fixed-group]]` or `[[linked-group]]` member written `cargo:foo` or `cargo/foo` resolves to package `foo` when a Cargo manifest declares `foo`, promoted or not, through the same selector resolver used for `--package` and changesets; a member naming an ecosystem with no such manifest fails loading with E108, and a bare member name ambiguous across ecosystems fails loading with E103 (not E108).",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-06",
      "criterion": "A changeset, `callisto add --package` or `callisto matrix --package` naming the bare name of promoted packages fails with E103 listing every qualified candidate and showing the qualified form to write; naming a package that does not exist under that name in that ecosystem fails with E102.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-07",
      "criterion": "A dependency edge is created only to a workspace package that declares the dependency's name in the depending manifest's own ecosystem; a name declared only in other ecosystems creates no edge and one `unknown-package` warning listing the candidates (`cargo:foo`), and an ordinary name no workspace package declares creates no edge and no diagnostic. An explicit pnpm `workspace:` reference that cannot resolve to an admitted npm member creates no edge and emits one `unknown-package` warning."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-10",
      "criterion": "For pnpm dependencies, Callisto preserves the declared key, target distribution name and exact `workspace:` suffix separately. `workspace:`, `workspace:*`, `workspace:^` and `workspace:~` are version-derived shorthands; aliases such as `workspace:foo@^1` resolve `foo` while retaining the declared key; relative references resolve only to the admitted npm member at the resolved directory. Catalog and opaque references are not guessed or rewritten."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-08",
      "criterion": "A package whose explicit `tag-template` equals another package's default tag template makes `status` and `version` fail with E101 naming both packages and the template.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-ID-09",
      "criterion": "A discovered package whose canonical manifests use different version grammars fails with E007 before version planning or init writes. This includes co-located Cargo.toml and pyproject.toml, whether the Python version is static or declared dynamic; matching numeric version strings do not bypass the grammar check.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-01",
      "criterion": "For each package, the first ecosystem-prefixed `[[package]]` rule whose ecosystem the package actually has a manifest in and whose name matches applies, regardless of declaration order relative to bare rules; a prefixed rule for an ecosystem the package has no manifest in never applies, even to a same-named package in another ecosystem. If no prefixed rule applies, the first matching bare rule applies."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-03",
      "criterion": "A bare `[[package]]` rule that would apply to a promoted package fails loading with E103 listing the qualified candidates; prefixed rules for the same packages load normally.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-04",
      "criterion": "A `[[package-set]]` rule applies only when no `[[package]]` rule matches, the first matching set in declaration order wins, and a `cargo:`/`cargo/`, `npm:`/`npm/` or `pypi:`/`pypi/` prefix restricts it to packages with a manifest in that ecosystem."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-05",
      "criterion": "A matched rule overrides only the fields it sets; otherwise a package uses release trigger `changeset`, `CHANGELOG.md` in its directory (a configured changelog is relative to the package directory), and the publish targets its manifests declare."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-06",
      "criterion": "A `publish-to` override whose target ecosystem is not among the matched package's manifest ecosystems fails loading with E119.",

    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-07",
      "criterion": "A `[[package-set]]` that matches no package emits one `package-set-matched-nothing` warning naming its pattern; a set matching a package that a `[[package]]` rule shadows counts as matched.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-08",
      "criterion": "A bare `[[package]]` rule matching packages whose manifests span two or more ecosystems, such as a dual-manifest package, emits one non-fatal `bare-rule-matches-multiple-ecosystems` warning; prefixed rules and `[[package-set]]` rules never emit it.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-CFG-09",
      "criterion": "A `[[package]]` rule that matches no package emits one `package-rule-matched-nothing` warning naming the rule.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-PLAT-01",
      "criterion": "A package.json with non-empty `os` and `cpu` arrays is an npm platform package whose platform and arch are the first entries; for Linux its ABI is `gnueabihf`, `gnu` or `musl` from the name's `-<abi>` suffix, otherwise none."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-PLAT-02",
      "criterion": "An npm-only platform package named in the `optionalDependencies` of exactly one admitted npm package becomes an attached platform package of that owner, inside or outside the npm workspace globs: it is not its own package and adds no publish targets to the owner."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-PLAT-03",
      "criterion": "A co-located platform manifest belongs to its directory's package, is never attached to another owner, and a `[[fixed-group]]` member may name any platform manifest by its own npm name."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-PLAT-04",
      "criterion": "When an owner is versioned or snapshotted, each attached platform manifest receives the owner's new version and the owner's `optionalDependencies` pins update to it, with no fixed group required."
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-PLAT-05",
      "criterion": "An admitted platform package named in no owner's or several owners' `optionalDependencies` stays its own package and emits a `platform-package-without-owner` warning with its manifest path and the owner count or paths.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "WS-PLAT-06",
      "criterion": "A platform package outside the npm workspace named by several owners emits `platform-package-without-owner` stating it is not released; one named by no owner stays undiscovered with no diagnostic.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "spec_file_path": "docs/specs/workspace.json"
}

      "criterion": "After `pre exit`, the next `version` moves every package at a prerelease version to its stable release (0.2.0-beta.1 becomes 0.2.0), consumes and deletes the pending changesets, and deletes `pre.json`."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-PRE-06",
      "criterion": "A malformed `.changeset/pre.json` (invalid JSON, a missing `mode`, `tag`, `initialVersions` or `changesets` field, a mode other than `pre` or `exit`, or an unparsable version) makes `version` fail with E114 and write nothing; an unreadable file fails with E115.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-PRE-07",
      "criterion": "`callisto snapshot --tag <tag>` sets every workspace package, and every attached platform package and fixed-group platform manifest, to a snapshot version built from the same tag and sha7 (the first 7 characters of HEAD) in the package's own grammar: `0.0.0-{tag}-{sha7}` for a SemVer package, `0.0.0.dev0+{tag}.{sha7}` for a Pep440 package; it fails if HEAD cannot be resolved."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-PRE-08",
      "criterion": "A snapshot writes manifests and refreshes each active ecosystem's existing lockfile, unconditionally (there is no `--no-refresh-lockfiles` for `snapshot`), so a subsequent locked install resolves against the snapshot version; it ignores and keeps pending changesets, writes no changelog or `pre.json`, and stages nothing in git; under `--dry-run` it writes nothing."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-PRE-09",
      "criterion": "For every workspace dependency whose current spec does not cover the snapshot version, `snapshot` rewrites that spec using the source declaration's manifest ecosystem and declared key or spelling, including Cargo aliases. Inherited Cargo declarations are rewritten in the workspace root rather than the member manifest. A spec that already covers the snapshot version is left unchanged."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-PRE-10",
      "criterion": "Every `pre.json` initial version is validated using the owning package's native grammar after historical and promoted identity resolution; the original JSON string is validated, not a spelling normalized by a cross-ecosystem fallback. A malformed owned baseline fails with E114 before version, changelog, pre-state or changeset writes during `version`, `pre exit` or resuming with `pre enter`."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-01",
      "criterion": "`version` writes the new version to every canonical manifest of a bumped package, so both manifests of a dual-manifest package move together."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-02",
      "criterion": "Before writing a package or platform manifest, apply reads its current version: equal to the planned `from` it is written, equal to the target it is left unchanged, so applying the same plan again is safe."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-03",
      "criterion": "A manifest whose current version is neither the planned `from` nor the target aborts apply with E117 naming the path, the found version and both expected versions.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-04",
      "criterion": "A manifest that receives a version bump and dependency rewrites in the same run is read once and written once with all changes, and a manifest already at its target with no rewrites is not rewritten. An owner's `optionalDependencies` pins, and edits to a workspace root `Cargo.toml` that is also a package manifest, are written separately."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-05",
      "criterion": "Files are written one at a time, each by atomic replacement, so an interrupted run never leaves a partially written file; a failing write stops the run and leaves earlier files in place."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-06",
      "criterion": "For each bumped package, apply prepends a `## {version}` section under the `# {package}` heading of its changelog (default `CHANGELOG.md` in the package directory, overridable with `changelog`), creating the file if missing and keeping CRLF line endings; a changelog that already has that heading is left unchanged."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-07",
      "criterion": "A changelog section lists each changeset summary as a bullet (continuation lines indented), an inferred bump as a commit subject with its short sha, a group bump as \"Released together with the `{group}` {fixed|linked} group.\", a new fixed-group member as \"Joined the `{group}` group at this version.\", a peer escalation as \"Peer dependency `{dep}` requires `{version}`\", and cascaded bumps as \"`{dep}` → `{version}`\" lines under a \"Dependency updates\" bullet."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-08",
      "criterion": "Outside pre mode, `version` refreshes affected lockfiles and stages written manifests, changelogs, `pre.json` changes and existing lockfiles before consuming release inputs. It stages consumed changeset and `pre.json` deletions via `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before unlinking those files from disk. If refresh, generated-state staging or input-deletion staging fails, changesets and pre-state deletion inputs remain on disk for retry."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-09",
      "criterion": "`version --dry-run` prints the computed plan (text output starts with `[DRY-RUN]`) and writes, deletes and stages nothing."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-10",
      "criterion": "`version --emit-decision <path>` writes the release decision JSON to `<path>` relative to the workspace root after the plan has been applied successfully: `schemaVersion` 2, a digest, and one entry per canonical manifest of each bumped package (ecosystem-qualified name, target version, reasons) sorted by package. Reason `kind` is `changeset`, `inference`, `fixedGroup` or `linkedGroup` (with `groupId`), `cascade` (with source package and edge kind, `peer` for peer escalation) or `preReleasePolicy` (with the prerelease tag)."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-11",
      "criterion": "`--emit-decision` with `--dry-run` is rejected before any work, and a plan with no bumps, or whose group members have different target versions, fails to produce a decision before any file is written.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-12",
      "criterion": "A diagnostic escalated to an error (for example `--strict` on the empty-changeset warning) is evaluated right after planning: `version` writes nothing -- not the manifests and changelog, not `pre.json`, not the `--emit-decision` file -- and exits with a failure status, instead of applying the plan and only then failing.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-13",
      "criterion": "Outside `mode: pre`, after planning but before any write, `version` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's on-disk effective version differs from its version at `HEAD`, or when its effective version staged in the git index differs from `HEAD`, provided a changeset remains in the `HEAD` tree or configured working-tree changesets directory (including untracked files), or a canonical manifest is staged. Staged metadata-only edits with unchanged effective versions are allowed. During `mode: exit`, already-written prerelease versions may be finalized to stable versions; a changed stable version is not exempt and is refused on retry. This detects interrupted applies without consuming retained inputs or stacking a second bump. E121 directs users to inspect staged and unstaged diffs; when outputs are verified as belonging to an interrupted apply, users finish removing its retained changeset or pre-state input with `git rm -- <path>` and commit, otherwise they commit intended version changes or restore affected files to `HEAD`. A repository with no commits yet, a manifest/changesets directory that didn't exist at `HEAD`, or an active `mode: pre` cycle (which legitimately reruns `version` without a commit in between) is not refused this way.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-14",
      "criterion": "By default, applying a plan refreshes and stages lockfiles for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write target, including all manifests of a dual-manifest package and workspace-root Cargo writes. It refreshes each existing lockfile: `cargo update --workspace` for Cargo; for Pypi, `uv lock` if `uv.lock` exists, else `poetry lock --no-update` if `poetry.lock` exists, else `pdm lock --update-reuse` if `pdm.lock` exists; for Npm, `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` for `package-lock.json`, `pnpm install --lockfile-only` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn install --mode update-lockfile` for `yarn.lock`, and `bun install --lockfile-only` for `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb`, each independently when its lockfile is present. `--no-refresh-lockfiles` skips refresh; applicable existing lockfiles are still staged."
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-15",
      "criterion": "A lockfile refresh command that exits non-zero aborts `version` with E208 naming the lockfile and the exact command that failed, instead of recording the failure and continuing.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "VER-APPLY-16",
      "criterion": "When E121 checks a staged canonical manifest outside prerelease mode, `version` compares its effective version in the Git index as well as the working tree against `HEAD`. It refuses if either copy contains an uncommitted version change, even when the other copy matches `HEAD`; staged metadata-only changes with the same effective version remain allowed.",

  "id": "SPEC-CLI",
  "purpose": "Defines the callisto command-line surface a user or CI script sees: commands, global flags, output formats, exit codes, and the behavior of status, add, init, pre, snapshot, completions and schema, plus the release workflow init generates.",

  "non_goals": [
    "Release planning, publishing and receipts behind `callisto release` and its hidden subcommands.",

    "Managed release-PR decisions made by the hidden `release-pr` plumbing."
  ],

    {
      "name": "version",

  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {

    },
    {

    },
    {
      "id": "CLI-SURF-06",
      "criterion": "`callisto help` prints the root help; `callisto help <command>` (nested names accepted as multiple words) prints that subcommand's help; an unknown command name exits 1 naming it. `callisto completions <shell>` never offers a hidden subcommand, at any nesting depth."
    },
    {
      "id": "CLI-SURF-04",

    {

    {

    },
    {

    {

    {
      "id": "CLI-OUT-05",
      "criterion": "With `--format json`, the status, add, init, pre and snapshot reports on stdout are single JSON objects with camelCase keys and a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` (the subcommand name) and `dryRun`."

      "id": "CLI-OUT-07",

    {

      "criterion": "Argument parsing errors (unknown flag, missing required argument, invalid value) exit 2 with clap's usage message; every other failure exits 1 and every success exits 0, including --dry-run previews and `release` reporting `Nothing to release.`",
      "is_error_case": true

    {
      "id": "CLI-OUT-09",
      "criterion": "`completions <shell>` and `schema` exit 0 without printing an error or panicking when stdout's reading end is already closed (e.g. piped into a command that exits early); a `--format json` report command's write error in that same situation propagates as `E213` and exits 1."
    },
    {
      "id": "CLI-STATUS-01",
      "criterion": "`callisto status`, with or without a callisto.toml, prints one row per package with its name, current version and planned bump (or `none`), then `<N> package(s) pending`, then a `Diagnostics:` section when any exist."

      "criterion": "A --package value missing `:severity`, with an unknown severity, or naming a package not in the workspace exits 1 and writes nothing; an unknown package name reports E102, and a bare name ambiguous across ecosystems reports E103 listing the qualified candidates.",

A spec that cannot be rewritten mechanically, such as an npm range with spaces, `||`, a hyphen or a wildcard, is left unchanged with a RangeNotRoundTrippable warning.
VER-CAS-07	A rewrite uses the source declaration's manifest ecosystem and preserves its declared dependency key or spelling, independent of either package's display prefix. A Cargo dependency's `package` name resolves its native target while edits retain its alias; inherited aliases resolve the workspace root's declaration. Python distribution names match using PEP 503 normalization while edits retain the spelling in the dependency declaration. A Cargo dependency inherited with `workspace = true` is rewritten in the workspace root's `[workspace.dependencies]`, not in the member manifest.
VER-PRE-09	For every workspace dependency whose current spec does not cover the snapshot version, `snapshot` rewrites that spec using the source declaration's manifest ecosystem and declared key or spelling, including Cargo aliases. Inherited Cargo declarations are rewritten in the workspace root rather than the member manifest. A spec that already covers the snapshot version is left unchanged.
VER-APPLY-08	Outside pre mode, `version` refreshes affected lockfiles and stages written manifests, changelogs, `pre.json` changes and existing lockfiles before consuming release inputs. It stages consumed changeset and `pre.json` deletions via `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before unlinking those files from disk. If refresh, generated-state staging or input-deletion staging fails, changesets and pre-state deletion inputs remain on disk for retry.
VER-APPLY-13	Outside `mode: pre`, after planning but before any write, `version` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's on-disk effective version differs from its version at `HEAD`, or when its effective version staged in the git index differs from `HEAD`, provided a changeset remains in the `HEAD` tree or configured working-tree changesets directory (including untracked files), or a canonical manifest is staged. Staged metadata-only edits with unchanged effective versions are allowed. During `mode: exit`, already-written prerelease versions may be finalized to stable versions; a changed stable version is not exempt and is refused on retry. This detects interrupted applies without consuming retained inputs or stacking a second bump. E121 directs users to inspect staged and unstaged diffs; when outputs are verified as belonging to an interrupted apply, users finish removing its retained changeset or pre-state input with `git rm -- <path>` and commit, otherwise they commit intended version changes or restore affected files to `HEAD`. CLI-INIT-04	The written callisto.toml starts with `# callisto configuration` and contains only answered intent: a `[[fixed-group]]` named `all` listing every non-platform package for fixed versioning, a `[[package]]` `tag-template` for each package whose existing tags follow a non-default convention, and, when shipping binaries, `publish-to` with `github-release` on the selected Cargo product plus a `[release]` table with `product-package`, `forge-repository` and one `[[release.artifact]]` per target and Cargo binary.
CLI-INIT-05	Tag detection matches each package's tags against its `{display id}@{version}` default, `{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}` and `v{version}`, and writes the single matching non-default convention as that package's tag-template.
CLI-INIT-06	init exits 1 without writing when a package matches more than one tag convention (listing each with its tags) or when more than one package matches `v{version}`.
CLI-INIT-07	After the config, init prints the first-release preview that `callisto release --dry-run` would show under it, or `No commits yet: commit, then run \`callisto release --dry-run\` to preview the first release.` when HEAD has no commit.
CLI-INIT-08	A successful init writes callisto.toml and creates .changeset/README.md only when it does not already exist.
CLI-INIT-09	init exits 1 without writing when callisto.toml already exists or when the directory is not inside a Git repository, each with a help line naming the fix. CLI-INIT-10	With a non-terminal stdin and no --yes, init exits 1 with `E240` naming --yes and every other missing flag; with --yes it exits 1 with `E241` naming each missing flag: --versioning always, --forge-repository when --artifact-target is given, and --product-package when --artifact-target is given and more than one supported Cargo package produces a binary.
CLI-INIT-11	With --yes, omitting --artifact-target writes no `[release]` table; --artifact-target is repeatable and comma-separated, and --workflow with --no-workflow exits 1 with `E242` before writing.

VER-CAS-05	Coverage: an exact spec covers only the equal version, a bare Cargo version is a caret requirement, a caret requirement never covers a prerelease, a Cargo `workspace = true` spec is tested using the root `[workspace.dependencies]` spec, and an npm `workspace:` shorthand (`workspace:`, `workspace:*`, `workspace:^` or `workspace:~`) always covers. A pnpm `workspace:` explicit range or exact version is tested using npm SemVer rules; an alias uses the range after its final `@`, and a relative path binds only to the admitted npm member at that directory. A catalog or other untestable spec is treated as covering and never rewritten; a catalog spec emits a CatalogSpecNotRewritten warning.
VER-CAS-06	A spec that no longer covers the new version is rewritten to it, keeping the operator and precision for Cargo and npm (`^1.2` becomes `^2.0` for 2.0.0), or to the exact version for npm when `preserve-npm-ranges = false`. A runtime, optional, build or peer dependent that is itself released in this run, for any reason, has every such spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the dependency's new version the same way, even when the spec still covers it; a dependent that is not releasing keeps its spec unless out of range. `workspace = true`, pnpm rolling `workspace:` shorthands and catalog specs are never rewritten by either rule; an out-of-range pnpm explicit range is rewritten while retaining its `workspace:` protocol and alias. A dev dependent's spec is rewritten only when out of range. A spec that cannot be rewritten mechanically, such as an npm range with spaces, `||`, a hyphen or a wildcard, is left unchanged with a RangeNotRoundTrippable warning.
VER-CAS-07	A rewrite uses the source declaration's manifest ecosystem and preserves its declared dependency key or spelling, independent of either package's display prefix. A Cargo dependency's `package` name resolves its native target while edits retain its alias; inherited aliases resolve the workspace root's declaration. Python distribution names match using PEP 503 normalization while edits retain the spelling in the dependency declaration. A Cargo dependency inherited with `workspace = true` is rewritten in the workspace root's `[workspace.dependencies]`, not in the member manifest.
VER-PRE-09	For every workspace dependency whose current spec does not cover the snapshot version, `snapshot` rewrites that spec using the source declaration's manifest ecosystem and declared key or spelling, including Cargo aliases. Inherited Cargo declarations are rewritten in the workspace root rather than the member manifest. A spec that already covers the snapshot version is left unchanged.
VER-APPLY-08	Outside pre mode, `version` refreshes affected lockfiles and stages written manifests, changelogs, `pre.json` changes and existing lockfiles before consuming release inputs. It stages consumed changeset and `pre.json` deletions via `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before unlinking those files from disk. If refresh, generated-state staging or input-deletion staging fails, changesets and pre-state deletion inputs remain on disk for retry.
VER-APPLY-13	Outside `mode: pre`, after planning but before any write, `version` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's on-disk effective version differs from its version at `HEAD`, or when its effective version staged in the git index differs from `HEAD`, provided a changeset remains in the `HEAD` tree or configured working-tree changesets directory (including untracked files), or a canonical manifest is staged. Staged metadata-only edits with unchanged effective versions are allowed. During `mode: exit`, already-written prerelease versions may be finalized to stable versions; a changed stable version is not exempt and is refused on retry. This detects interrupted applies without consuming retained inputs or stacking a second bump. E121 directs users to inspect staged and unstaged diffs; when outputs are verified as belonging to an interrupted apply, users finish removing its retained changeset or pre-state input with `git rm -- <path>` and commit, otherwise they commit intended version changes or restore affected files to `HEAD`. A repository with no commits yet, a manifest/changesets directory that didn't exist at `HEAD`, or an active `mode: pre` cycle (which legitimately reruns `version` without a commit in between) is not refused this way.
CLI-INIT-01	Before any question, `callisto init` prints `Detected:` with the ecosystems, the origin remote URL, and each package's qualified id, version, last tag, and executable names for executable-producing packages. Artifact selection includes only supported Cargo binary targets.
CLI-INIT-02	Interactive init asks only: versioning (independent or fixed); whether to ship Cargo binaries as GitHub release assets, only when a supported Cargo binary target exists; the product package, only when more than one Cargo package produces a binary; the forge repository, pre-filled from origin; comma-separated target triples; whether to generate a workflow (default no); and whether to write callisto.toml (default yes).
CLI-INIT-03	A supplied flag (--versioning, --artifact-target, --product-package, --forge-repository, --workflow, --no-workflow) skips its question, and declining the final write question writes no file.
CLI-INIT-04	The written callisto.toml starts with `# callisto configuration` and contains only answered intent: a `[[fixed-group]]` named `all` listing every non-platform package for fixed versioning, a `[[package]]` `tag-template` for each package whose existing tags follow a non-default convention, and, when shipping binaries, `publish-to` with `github-release` on the selected Cargo product plus a `[release]` table with `product-package`, `forge-repository` and one `[[release.artifact]]` per target and Cargo binary.
CLI-INIT-05	Tag detection matches each package's tags against its `{display id}@{version}` default, `{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}` and `v{version}`, and writes the single matching non-default convention as that package's tag-template.
CLI-INIT-06	init exits 1 without writing when a package matches more than one tag convention (listing each with its tags) or when more than one package matches `v{version}`.
CLI-INIT-07	After the config, init prints the first-release preview that `callisto release --dry-run` would show under it, or `No commits yet: commit, then run \`callisto release --dry-run\` to preview the first release.` when HEAD has no commit.
CLI-INIT-08	A successful init writes callisto.toml and creates .changeset/README.md only when it does not already exist.
CLI-INIT-09	init exits 1 without writing when callisto.toml already exists or when the directory is not inside a Git repository, each with a help line naming the fix. With no `origin` remote configured, init instead writes callisto.toml, skips the workflow and shipping-binaries questions, and emits an `init-origin-missing` warning diagnostic; `--workflow` or `--artifact-target` without `origin` exits 1 naming the fix, and `callisto release` refuses later.
CLI-INIT-10	With a non-terminal stdin and no --yes, init exits 1 with `E240` naming --yes and every other missing flag; with --yes it exits 1 with `E241` naming each missing flag: --versioning always, --forge-repository when --artifact-target is given, and --product-package when --artifact-target is given and more than one supported Cargo package produces a binary.
CLI-INIT-11	With --yes, omitting --artifact-target writes no `[release]` table; --artifact-target is repeatable and comma-separated, and --workflow with --no-workflow exits 1 with `E242` before writing.

content.text:
Review verdict: **changes requested**. I found three implementation issues and one material verification gap in the requested T04/T10 scope.

1. **P2 — `init` can mistake a non-Cargo executable for a Cargo artifact.** [`init.rs`](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:235) combines executable names from every manifest in a package, while [`supports_artifact_builder`](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:65) infers support solely from the package’s qualified ID. A dual-manifest package with a Cargo library and an npm `bin` is therefore treated as a Cargo binary package. `init --artifact-target` can select it and generate an artifact build for a binary Cargo does not provide.
